questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que período aconteceu a Guerra do Paraguai?
questions.hint: Ela ocorreu durante o Segundo Reinado no Brasil.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quais países formaram a Tríplice Aliança?
questions.answer: Brasil, Argentina e Uruguai
questions.hint: Pense nos vizinhos do Paraguai na região do Rio da Prata.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem governava o Brasil durante a Guerra do Paraguai?
questions.answer: Uma monarquia, com um imperador
questions.hint: A República só foi proclamada em 1889.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chamou a aliança formada contra o Paraguai em 1865?
questions.answer: Tríplice Aliança
questions.hint: O nome indica que eram três países.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual fato ajudou a iniciar o conflito em 1864?
options: A Argentina invadiu o Rio de Janeiro
O Uruguai fechou o porto de Santos
O Paraguai apreendeu um navio brasileiro no rio Paraguai
O Brasil declarou independência de Portugal
questions.answer: O Paraguai apreendeu um navio brasileiro no rio Paraguai
questions.hint: O episódio aconteceu em um rio, pouco depois de o Brasil intervir no Uruguai.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual província brasileira foi invadida por tropas paraguaias no início da guerra?
questions.answer: Mato Grosso
questions.hint: Procure a província que faz fronteira com o Paraguai.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que a navegação dos rios da bacia do Prata era tão importante na época?
options: Ligava diretamente o Brasil à Europa por terra
Era o único lugar onde se plantava café
Servia apenas para o lazer das famílias ricas
Era a principal ligação de regiões do interior com o oceano e o comércio
questions.answer: Era a principal ligação de regiões do interior com o oceano e o comércio
questions.hint: O Paraguai não tem litoral.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual era o nome dos batalhões criados em 1865 para aumentar o exército brasileiro?
questions.answer: Voluntários da Pátria
questions.hint: O nome sugere pessoas que se alistavam para defender o país.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual batalha naval de 1865 deu à Tríplice Aliança o controle dos rios?
questions.answer: Batalha do Riachuelo
questions.hint: Foi travada no rio Paraná, perto de Corrientes.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como muitas pessoas escravizadas participaram da guerra pelo lado brasileiro?
options: Foram proibidas de chegar perto das tropas
Foram enviadas ao combate, algumas com a promessa de liberdade
questions.answer: Foram enviadas ao combate, algumas com a promessa de liberdade
questions.hint: A escravidão no Brasil só terminou em 1888.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual foi uma das consequências da guerra para o Paraguai?
options: Grande perda de população e de território
Conquista de uma saída para o mar
questions.answer: Grande perda de população e de território
questions.hint: Lembre que o país foi o derrotado e a guerra aconteceu em grande parte no seu solo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual foi uma das consequências da guerra para o Brasil?
options: Aumento da dívida externa e fortalecimento do Exército
Perda do território de Mato Grosso
questions.answer: Aumento da dívida externa e fortalecimento do Exército
questions.hint: A guerra foi muito cara e deu mais prestígio aos militares.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Depois da guerra, muitos militares brasileiros passaram a:
options: Defender a volta do domínio português
Ter mais peso na política e criticar a monarquia
Mudar-se para o Paraguai em massa
questions.answer: Ter mais peso na política e criticar a monarquia
questions.hint: Pense no que aconteceu no Brasil em 1889.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique duas causas da Guerra do Paraguai, ligando-as à disputa pela região do Rio da Prata.
questions.hint: Pense em rios, fronteiras e influência sobre o Uruguai.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que a Guerra do Paraguai é considerada um dos conflitos mais trágicos da América do Sul? Justifique com um exemplo.
questions.hint: Considere as perdas humanas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como a participação de pessoas escravizadas na guerra pode ter contribuído para o debate sobre a abolição no Brasil?
questions.hint: Pense em quem lutou pelo país e no que recebeu em troca.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is JavaScript mainly used for on a web page?
options: Storing the website on a server
questions.answer: Adding interactivity
questions.hint: HTML gives structure and CSS gives style.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does DOM stand for?
questions.answer: Document Object Model
questions.hint: It describes how a browser represents a page.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which HTML tag is used to add JavaScript to a web page?
questions.answer: <script>
questions.hint: Its name is another word for a program's code.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In web programming, what is an event?
options: Something that happens, such as a click or a key press
questions.answer: Something that happens, such as a click or a key press
questions.hint: Think about what a user does on a page.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which line finds the element with the id "score"?
questions.answer: document.getElementById("score")
questions.hint: The name of the method says what it gets.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which keyword is used to define a function in JavaScript?
questions.answer: function
questions.hint: The keyword is the same word as the concept.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which line makes the function "greet" run when a button called btn is clicked?
questions.answer: btn.addEventListener("click", greet);
questions.hint: You are adding something that listens for an event.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which property changes the text inside an element?
questions.answer: textContent
questions.hint: The property name includes the word for what is being changed.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which event name is used to respond to a key being pressed down?
questions.answer: keydown
questions.hint: It joins two English words: key and a direction.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A page runs: let count = 0; Each click on a button runs count = count + 2; What is count after 3 clicks?
questions.hint: Work through the clicks one at a time.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A page runs: let total = 10; A button click runs total = total - 3; What is total after 2 clicks?
questions.hint: Subtract once for every click.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What will this code display in the alert? let name = "Sol"; alert("Hi " + name);
questions.answer: Hi Sol
questions.hint: The + joins two strings, and name is a variable.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A programmer writes btn.addEventListener("click", greet()); with brackets after greet. What is the problem?
options: The button is deleted from the page
greet runs straight away instead of waiting for the click
Nothing is wrong with this code
questions.answer: greet runs straight away instead of waiting for the click
questions.hint: Brackets call a function immediately.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In this code, what does the DOM let JavaScript do? document.getElementById("msg").textContent = "Well done!";
options: Change the file saved on the server
Change the page after it has loaded
questions.answer: Change the page after it has loaded
questions.hint: The HTML file itself is not rewritten.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why a web developer uses a function to handle a button click instead of writing the code directly in the page.
questions.hint: Think about reuse and about when the code should run.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe the steps needed to make a button change the text of a paragraph when clicked.
questions.hint: Think about finding elements, listening and changing the content.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main purpose of an individual presentation?
options: To share researched ideas clearly with an audience
To answer a written exam paper
To read out a text word for word
questions.answer: To share researched ideas clearly with an audience
questions.hint: Think about who is listening.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What word describes the people listening to a presentation?
questions.answer: audience
questions.hint: A speaker should adapt their talk to these people.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the best source for researching a presentation?
options: A guess based on the title
A reliable website checked against other sources
questions.answer: A reliable website checked against other sources
questions.hint: Good research can be checked.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What are cue cards for?
options: To hold key points that prompt the speaker
To be read aloud word by word
To hand to the audience as a test
questions.answer: To hold key points that prompt the speaker
questions.hint: They should help you look up, not down.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which phrase is a signpost at the start of a new section?
options: Moving on to my second point,
questions.answer: Moving on to my second point,
questions.hint: Signposts show listeners where the talk is going.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why does a speaker make eye contact with the audience?
options: To show confidence and keep listeners engaged
questions.answer: To show confidence and keep listeners engaged
questions.hint: Consider how it feels to be looked at by a speaker.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What term means the speed at which someone speaks?
questions.answer: pace
questions.hint: A good speaker varies it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the effect of a short pause after an important point?
options: It shows the speaker has failed
It makes the talk sound rushed
It tells listeners the talk is over
It gives the audience time to take in the idea
questions.answer: It gives the audience time to take in the idea
questions.hint: Silence can give weight to words.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a rhetorical question?
options: A question at the end of a test
A question asked for effect, not for an answer
A question that the audience must answer in writing
questions.answer: A question asked for effect, not for an answer
questions.hint: Think about "Who wants to live in a polluted town?"

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which version uses Standard English suitable for a formal presentation?
options: Loads of people reckon it's well bad.
Many people believe this is a serious problem.
Like, people think it's dodgy, innit.
questions.answer: Many people believe this is a serious problem.
questions.hint: Look for formal vocabulary and full grammar.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A member of the audience asks something you cannot answer. What is the best response?
options: Tell them the question is silly
Be honest and offer to find out
questions.answer: Be honest and offer to find out
questions.hint: Honesty protects your credibility.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the strongest opening for a presentation on plastic waste?
options: Imagine a rubbish truck emptying into the sea every minute.
I didn't have time to practise this.
My talk is about some stuff on plastic.
questions.answer: Imagine a rubbish truck emptying into the sea every minute.
questions.hint: A strong opening grabs attention.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why should a speaker rehearse aloud before a presentation?
options: To check timing and how the words sound
To learn to speak as fast as possible
questions.answer: To check timing and how the words sound
questions.hint: Reading silently will not reveal this.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why should slides contain only a few words?
options: So the speaker can read every line from them
So the audience listens rather than reads
So nobody needs to look at them
So the talk needs no structure
questions.answer: So the audience listens rather than reads
questions.hint: Think about where the audience's attention goes.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain two ways a speaker can use their voice to keep an audience interested.
questions.hint: Think about pace, volume and tone.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why is it important to prepare for questions from the audience? Give one way of doing this.
questions.hint: Consider which parts of your topic might raise doubts.
